assessment: A circa-2015-era GoDaddy Website Builder site: fixed pixel-position layout, decorative script webfonts, and a dead 'View on Mobile' link — content is genuinely strong (35+ years, licensed, real reviews) but presentation reads as dated and not mobile-responsive.
strengths: Strong real content: 35+ years experience, license number stated (PA088400), clear service breakdown across 4 categories
8 real, specific named client testimonials with genuine detail (not generic 5-star filler)
Genuine technical FAQ content about concrete (control joints, rebar, sealing) — shows real expertise
Clear phone number and email presented prominently in the header
weaknesses: No responsive/mobile layout: everything is absolutely positioned with hardcoded pixel coordinates typical of GoDaddy's legacy "Website Builder" (not its newer editor), and no <meta name="viewport"> tag was found
'View on Mobile' link is dead — onclick="return false;" — a leftover control that does nothing
No HTTPS on the primary domain (http://masonryplus.net); browsers will flag it as Not Secure

Decorative cursive/handwriting webfonts (Allura, Arizonia, Amatic SC) loaded alongside plain body text — inconsistent typographic system typical of a builder's default font library rather than an intentional brand choice
No schema.org / JSON-LD structured data found — invisible to AI answer engines and weak for local SEO
No dedicated service-area pages — service area is only mentioned as a text string in the header/footer
Native HTML contact form only, no CRM/lead-routing integration detected
Copyright footer still reads "1999" with no recent update, reinforcing a dated first impression
anti_patterns_observed: Absolute pixel-position layout instead of responsive flow
Decorative script fonts used inconsistently across headings
overall: Strong candidate for redesign — genuinely good, expert content trapped in a non-responsive 2015-era GoDaddy builder site with no HTTPS and no structured data.
